scope: Theorem 1.2 (Finite conditional resolution) of the manuscript “Buffered comparison and stopping-band resolution in critical Ising” (preprints/Buffered-comparison-and-stopping-band-resolution-in-critical-Ising-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d5167e3fe5fb85f4), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix the preceding band geometry and use the critical plus-boundary law in a larger reference square. For every ϵ, η > 0, one can choose contour levels in any prescribed separated subwindows, a finite descriptor Zδ ∈ {0, 1, . . . , m}, and regular signed barriers Γ1, . . . , Γm with the following properties for all sufficiently fine meshes. The exceptional state 0 has probability at most ϵ. For every transcript in a good state i ∈ {1, . . . , m}, insert the plus pins of Γi and then its minus pins. The sum of the two resulting total-variation changes on the target is at most η. The final target-side law Qi,δ is the same for every transcript in that state. Consequently this conclusion holds simultaneously for all bounded target observables, including mesh-dependent observables. For any fixed finite list of bands the descriptors have convergent joint laws. The finite list of barriers and its positive geometric clearances are chosen before the mesh threshold. If another law has band density at most K times the reference density, its exceptional probability is at most Kϵ.
